title: Part Eighteen: The Verdict: Illusion, Mechanism or Promise?

sections.brief: Master told-vs-record ledger in three tables, fifteen mechanisms (mobility, wages, unions/buybacks, minimum wage, housing, education, health, debt, retirement, taxes/fees, wealth, groups, poverty/justice, rules/lobbying, belief): as taught (sourced), the record with key figure, designed vs captured friction, who gains / who pays, register (documented / disputed / not supported); the circulating claims that did not survive; where the promise works. Figures: compare (three ledger tables, told vs record); stats (registers and corrected claims)

Protocol 2B.13 scorecard for seven promises (better life than parents, home, secure job, health care, college as ladder, secure retirement, fair rules): sub-scores fulfilment (status 0-4), breadth (group ratio rule), reach trend (change rule), durability (legal-backing rule), each sourced; weights 40/30/20/10 disclosed; arithmetic shown; aggregate 4.7/10 labelled editorial synthesis; fulfilment-only 5.7; equal-weight test 4.6; costs and distribution reported not scored; holds / holds for some / falls short. Figures: flow (method); compare (scorecard table with sub-scores); stats (aggregates and tests)

Documented levers with evidence for and against, status Oct 2026: 2021 CTC (SPM child poverty 5.2% to 12.4%; Ananat et al. vs Corinth et al.); auto-enrolment (94 vs 64%; SECURE 2.0); minimum wage (Cengiz et al.; Neumark-Shirley; CBO 1.4m/900,000); Medicaid expansion (Miller et al. 9.4%, Oregon experiment, Bjoerkheim; NHIS 18.1 vs 9.0); Minneapolis supply reforms (Pew; Axios caveats); bankruptcy (2022 attestation 98% vs 9.3m defaults; 2005 change; state medical-debt laws); CT baby bonds (Zewde vs Bruenig); labelled Interpretation, not finding (Sophia illusion thesis) with counter-readings; closing in three registers. Figures: compare (levers: evidence for/against/status); time (levers enacted and reversed)
